payload.writeUp: Claude Code research, 23 Oct 2026: recent UK accelerator and pre-seed programme investments (mainly Carbon13 SEIS funds, Antler UK's October 2026 batch, Haatch and SFC Capital). Programmes keep live deal flow behind investor logins, so only two companies here state they are raising now; the rest are early-stage companies whose next round is expected, reachable by founder intro. SEIS/EIS status is unknown for all: no page read states HMRC advance assurance, although SEIS funds invested in several (noted per company). Every UK location was checked on Companies House.

candidate.name: COOloop
candidate.teaser: Catalyst platform turning captured CO2 and green hydrogen into e-ethanol; founders say they are raising now and want angels.
candidate.description: COOloop is developing a metal-organic framework catalyst that converts CO2 and hydrogen directly into e-ethanol, with a licensing model aimed first at bioethanol producers. CEO Ike Omambala (20+ years at BP, INEOS and in chemicals leadership per Carbon13) and CTO Dr Raj Lakshman (co-inventor of the catalyst) came through the Carbon13 Venture Builder, which invested via its SEIS Fund VIII in May 2026. Carbon13 reported $200K of funding to date and a goal of reaching TRL5 (500+ hours of catalyst stability). In an interview published 21 Oct 2026 the founders said they are raising in the current round and particularly want angels with chemical-engineering experience. Main risks: lab-stage chemistry, long industrial sales cycles, round size and terms not disclosed.
candidate.discoverySignal: Carbon13 founder interview (21 Oct 2026): "we're raising in this current round", seeking angels.
candidate.researchRuleMatched: Accelerator alumnus raising now with a founder route; SEIS-fund backed at pre-seed.

founders.name: Ike Omambala
founders.bio: 20+ years with BP, INEOS and in chemical business leadership, per Carbon13.

founders.name: Dr Raj Lakshman
founders.bio: Co-inventor of COOloop's catalyst with expertise in CO2 conversion and reactor design, per Carbon13.

access.notes: Founders said on 21 Oct 2026 they are raising and want angels; site has an investor-inquiry form and says "Interested in partnering or investing? Email us at info@cooloop.tech". Carbon13 also shares deals with its investor community.

eis.note: Carbon13 invested through its SEIS Fund VIII (May 2026). Whether the current round offers SEIS or EIS relief is not stated.

openQuestions: Round size, valuation and instrument (SEIS/EIS-compatible equity?)
Path and cost from TRL5 to a pilot with a bioethanol producer

assessment.summary: Live raise with an explicit ask for angels and a credible industrial team, but very early chemistry with no disclosed terms.
whyInterested: Experienced industry CEO plus catalyst inventor
risks: Round size and valuation not disclosed
assessment.bullCase: A working MOF catalyst for direct CO2-to-ethanol could license widely into fuels and SAF markets.
assessment.bearCase: Catalyst stability or economics fail at scale, and the company needs far more capital than angels can supply.
assessment.whyNow: They are raising now (Oct 2026) and want angels; Carbon13 SEIS Fund backing suggests an early, low entry point.
openQuestions: Current round size, terms and SEIS/EIS status
assessment.nextAction: Email info@cooloop.tech asking for the deck, round terms and SEIS/EIS status.

candidate.name: Viridys Bio
candidate.teaser: Colour-changing biosensors that warn growers of crop stress before symptoms show; SFC-led pre-seed left open for more investors.
candidate.description: Viridys Bio makes low-cost, non-living biosensor devices that detect volatile organic compounds emitted by stressed plants, starting with glasshouse tomatoes. CEO Stuart Dixon (ex-Goldman Sachs, per the company site) and CTO Dr Rotem Berman (biosensor developer) went through Carbon13, which invested via SEIS Fund IX. On 4 June 2026 the company announced the first close of a £500k pre-seed led by SFC Capital, with Carbon13 and angels, and said the round remained open with about £130k available for additional investors. Carbon13 reported £792k raised across grants and equity by Oct 2026. Risks: pre-prototype hardware, agricultural sales cycles, and the open allocation may now be filled.
candidate.discoverySignal: Company press release (4 Jun 2026): round remains open with ~£130k for additional investors.
candidate.researchRuleMatched: SFC-led pre-seed with spare allocation for angels; accelerator alumnus.

founders.name: Stuart Dixon
founders.bio: 11 years at Goldman Sachs; MBA and biotechnology masters, per company site.

founders.name: Dr Rotem Berman
founders.bio: Biosensor developer who pioneered a real-world biosensor deployment, per company site.

access.notes: 4 Jun 2026 release said ~£130k remained for a limited number of additional investors. Status in Oct 2026 unconfirmed; contact the CEO directly.

eis.note: Carbon13 invested via SEIS Fund IX and the lead (SFC) backs SEIS-eligible first rounds; the company does not state SEIS/EIS for this round.

openQuestions: Is any of the ~£130k still available in Oct 2026?
Pre-money valuation of the SFC-led round
Timeline for the first tomato prototype and paid pilots

assessment.summary: A documented open allocation in an SFC-led pre-seed is a rare concrete route in, though it may since have filled.
whyInterested: Company stated spare allocation for new investors
Third-party NIAB study cited by Carbon13
risks: Allocation may have closed since June
assessment.bullCase: Cheap, sticker-like sensors could cut pesticide use across glasshouses and win distribution through grower partners.
assessment.bearCase: Sensitivity in real glasshouses disappoints and growers will not pay enough for a low-cost consumable.
assessment.whyNow: Round was left open for extra investors; Carbon13 profiled the company on 6 Oct 2026.
assessment.nextAction: Email Stuart Dixon to ask whether the pre-seed allocation is still open and on what terms.

candidate.name: Climingo
candidate.teaser: Independent marketplace that benchmarks weather forecasters for energy, insurance and construction buyers.
candidate.description: Climingo lets organisations evaluate weather and climate forecast providers at their own locations for free, earning a fee from the winning provider when the customer buys. CEO Dr Avi Baruch previously co-founded a flood-forecasting company and took it to Series A; CTO Alper Dincer has 20+ years in geospatial platforms (per Carbon13). It raised £290,000 led by Carbon13 (SEIS Fund IX) with One Planet Capital and Innovate UK, announced 27 Aug 2026, and has its first organisation signed up. The CEO referred to talking to investors for a future round. Risks: marketplace depends on provider cooperation, tiny current traction, next round timing not stated.
candidate.discoverySignal: Carbon13 announced the £290k raise on 27 Aug 2026; company is in Carbon13's 12-month Growth Phase.
candidate.researchRuleMatched: SEIS-fund-backed accelerator company with a founder route ahead of its next round.

founders.bio: Former academic; co-founded a flood-forecasting company and took it from zero to Series A.

founders.name: Alper Dincer
founders.bio: 20+ years architecting geospatial and environmental monitoring platforms, per Carbon13.

access.notes: Pre-seed closed Aug 2026. Contact founders (site phone/contact form) or Carbon13's investor community (investors@carbonthirteen.com) about the next round.

eis.note: Carbon13's investment came from its SEIS Fund IX; SEIS/EIS for a future round not stated.

facts.label: Pre-seed (Aug 2026)
facts.value: £290,000 led by Carbon13 with One Planet Capital and Innovate UK

facts.label: Business model
facts.value: Free evaluation for customers; winning provider pays Climingo on procurement

openQuestions: When the next round opens and its size
Do forecast providers accept the fee model?

assessment.summary: Repeat founder and tidy business model, but the round just closed and traction is one organisation.
whyInterested: CEO has taken a climate-data company to Series A
SEIS-fund-backed at a small round size
risks: Just closed; next round timing unknown
assessment.bullCase: Becomes the default independent benchmark for procuring weather data across energy and insurance.
assessment.bearCase: Large forecasters or data platforms bundle benchmarking themselves and buyers will not switch.
assessment.whyNow: Fresh Carbon13 graduate in its Growth Phase; good time to build a relationship before the seed.
assessment.nextAction: Ask Carbon13 investor team or the CEO to be added to the next round's investor list.

candidate.name: HexSeed Technology
candidate.subSector: Diamond thermal coatings for GaN chips
candidate.teaser: Low-temperature lab-grown diamond coatings, made from captured CO2, to cool GaN power chips in AI data centres.
candidate.description: HexSeed is developing a low-temperature process to grow diamond directly onto finished gallium-nitride power devices, working with University of Bristol researchers, with diamond made from captured CO2. Founded in late 2025 by CEO Mark Tandy (CCUS background), CTO Dr Leonardo Santoni (UCL chemistry PhD) and Dr Michael Glerum (Cambridge engineering PhD). Carbon13 invested from SEIS Fund IX; with Net Zero Technology Centre and Vento the company reported just over £600k and about 12+ months of runway, plus a conditional Innovate UK grant. Plan: proof of concept, then a low-capex pilot and licensing to fabs. Risks: hard semiconductor process science, long qualification cycles, round just closed.
candidate.discoverySignal: £600k+ raise reported 21 Aug 2026 after Carbon13 Cohort 9.
candidate.researchRuleMatched: SEIS-fund-backed deep-tech accelerator company; founder route for next round.

founders.name: Mark Tandy
founders.bio: 20+ years in energy, the last five in carbon capture, utilisation and storage.

founders.name: Dr Leonardo Santoni
founders.bio: UCL chemistry PhD in precursor design for metal deposition and crystal growth.

founders.name: Dr Michael Glerum
founders.bio: Cambridge engineering PhD; built and ran a carbon-nanotube pilot plant.

access.notes: Round closed Aug 2026 with 12+ months runway. Route is a founder intro or Carbon13's investor community (investors@carbonthirteen.com) ahead of the next round.

eis.note: Carbon13 invested via SEIS Fund IX; scheme status of later rounds not stated.

facts.value: Just over £600,000 incl. Carbon13, NZTC and Vento; ~12+ months runway

facts.label: Registered company
facts.value: HEXSEED TECHNOLOGY LIMITED, SC871246, Banchory, Scotland

openQuestions: Proof-of-concept milestones on commercial GaN devices
IP position vs. University of Bristol

assessment.summary: Strong technical team in a hot thermal-management niche, but the round just closed and science risk is high.
whyInterested: AI data-centre cooling is a pressing market
assessment.bullCase: Licensable diamond-on-GaN coating becomes an industry standard for power devices.
assessment.bearCase: Coating fails reliability tests or incumbents solve thermal limits another way.
assessment.whyNow: Funded for ~12 months; relationship-building now positions the family for the next round.
assessment.nextAction: Request an intro via Carbon13 investor team to track milestones before the next raise.

candidate.name: mushroom+
candidate.teaser: Synthetic-biology platform engineering whole fresh mushrooms with around 10x the protein, licensed via spawn makers.
candidate.description: mushroom+ uses molecular mycology to raise the natural protein content of whole fresh mushrooms (target 10x, comparable to meat) rather than making a processed meat alternative. Founders Dr Corinne Pinder and Dr Ressa Lebedinec are molecular-mycology PhDs with 20+ years combined fungal-biotech experience (per Carbon13). Carbon13 invested via SEIS Fund IX; an Aug 2026 interview describes a low-capex model partnering with leading spawn companies and partnership negotiations. No live round is stated. Risks: regulatory treatment of engineered food in the UK/EU, consumer acceptance, early science.
candidate.discoverySignal: Carbon13 SEIS Fund IX investment (Jul 2026) and founder interview (6 Aug 2026).

founders.name: Dr Corinne Pinder
founders.bio: Molecular mycology PhD; fungal biotech experience incl. strain engineering.

founders.name: Dr Ressa Lebedinec

access.notes: No live round stated. Contact founders via hello@mushroomplus.co.uk or Carbon13's investor community.

assessment.bullCase: A protein-dense whole mushroom licensed through incumbent spawn producers reaches global scale cheaply.
assessment.bearCase: Regulation or taste/texture trade-offs stall commercialisation.
assessment.whyNow: Recently backed; partnership negotiations under way.
assessment.nextAction: Low priority: email founders to ask about next-round timing.

candidate.name: TeraSort
candidate.teaser: Drop-in, fully robotic modular waste-sorting units claiming large capex and opex cuts; piloted at Latitude festival.
candidate.description: TeraSort builds standalone, end-to-end robotic sorting modules that turn collected waste into single-material outputs, using low-cost robots and AI vision. CEO Johnny Longden and CTO Dr Phil Worthington (3x founder, 20 years in computer vision per Carbon13) came through Carbon13, which invested via SEIS Fund VIII in May 2026. Carbon13 claims capex cuts up to 10x and opex up to 5x; an 8-robot system ran for five days at Latitude festival and a pilot at a London urban development is under way. No live round stated. Risks: hardware reliability on messy waste, capital needs, competition from established sorting-robot makers.
candidate.discoverySignal: Founder interview published by Carbon13 on 13 Oct 2026 after a festival pilot.
candidate.researchRuleMatched: SEIS-fund-backed accelerator company with pilots; founder route.

founders.bio: Three-time founder with 20 years in computer vision and AI, incl. recycling.

candidate.name: Pure Capture Innovations
candidate.teaser: Biochar composite adsorbents as a drop-in replacement for activated carbon to remove short-chain PFAS from water.
candidate.description: Pure Capture Innovations develops biochar-molecular filter composites intended to replace coal-based granular activated carbon and capture short-chain PFAS and other micropollutants in water treatment. CEO Mark Wild has 25+ years in advanced materials and CTO Dr Usman Shoukat 15 years in biochar materials (per Carbon13). Carbon13 invested via SEIS Fund VIII; a Sept 2026 article cites a £530,000 raise including grants. The CEO said they aim to be ready by 2027 for the next step in funding, paid pilots and IP development. Risks: water-utility procurement is slow, technical validation pending, licensing model unproven.

candidate.teaser: Robot-agnostic software layer to deploy and distribute embodied AI across different robots and compute.
candidate.description: Kinematic Trees builds nature-inspired, robot-agnostic deployment software ("universal comms, control and computation") for robots in manufacturing, agriculture, construction and healthcare. CEO Dr Stuart Wilson is a senior lecturer in computational neuroscience at the University of Sheffield; CTO Daniel Camilleri previously co-founded and exited Cyberselves Universal (per The AI Insider). In July 2026 it raised £585,000 pre-seed from Haatch's SEIS Fund, the D2N2 Early-Stage Angel Investment Fund and the British Business Bank Syndicate Fund, and planned first factory deployment partnerships in H2 2026. Risks: horizontal robotics software is hard to monetise, academic-led team, no current round.

candidate.name: Pontiro
candidate.subSector: Medical imaging anonymisation and AI evaluation
candidate.teaser: NHS-used imaging anonymisation and independent evaluation of healthcare AI, from the Alacrity Foundation accelerator.
candidate.description: Pontiro provides on-premise anonymisation of medical images and reports so hospitals can share data for research and AI, and is launching an independent AI evaluation platform for hospitals and vendors. Co-founders Lewis Bowen, Evan Jenkins and Adam Shannon are Alacrity Foundation alumni. Alacrity reports more than 2 million images processed across NHS Wales and a £357,500 round led by SFC Capital and the British Business Bank with Plug and Play Ventures (Feb 2026), to expand into NHS England and launch AI evaluation in 2026. No live round stated. Risks: slow NHS procurement, competition in de-identification, small team.
